name: Mu-Tron Bi-Phase
originalPurpose: A large, two-channel phaser from the American company Musitronics, designed by Mike Beigel and sold to guitarists and keyboard players. A phaser makes a sweeping, whooshing sound by mixing a signal with a slightly shifted copy of itself.
whatActuallyHappened: At the Black Ark, Lee Perry put whole mixes through it and swept it by hand while the tape was running. Cymbals, hi-hats and sometimes entire rhythm tracks swirl and swoosh as though passing through a jet engine. On his mid-1970s productions the phaser is not decoration added at the end. It is something he played.
priceStory: Around 280 US dollars new, a serious price for an effects unit, aimed at professional players. Accounts of the Black Ark say Perry acquired his early, which is part of why the sound was so unusual in Kingston at the time.
hook: A whooshing effect box that Lee Perry played by hand across whole mixes.

blurb.age7: A machine that makes a whooshing sound, like a jet plane flying past, which Lee Perry used on his records.
blurb.age13: A phaser makes music sound like it is swirling or whooshing past. Most people used it on a guitar. Lee Perry ran whole songs through it and turned the knobs by hand while the music played, so the hi-hats and cymbals swoosh back and forth. Once you hear it on one of his records you start hearing it everywhere in his music.
blurb.adult: The phaser is one of the most recognisable signatures of Perry's Black Ark period. Some accounts name the model only as 'a Mu-Tron phaser', and the Bi-Phase is the one most sources identify. The larger point holds either way: Perry, like King Tubby, treated studio processing as live performance rather than as a setting.
